B. Is this measure already running in Vantaa and Kerava wellbeing services county (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how much?
Measure: Nurse navigator for every suspected lung cancer. A named nurse books and chases every test, calls the patient, prepares the MDT and removes waiting between steps from referral to first treatment.
supported_en: The 2026 scoping review of 13 studies (Japan Journal of Nursing Science) links cancer patient navigation to an earlier start of first treatment.
not_supported_en: No page shows a measured reduction compared with usual care, or the 15% (0–30%) we assume for lung cancer.
summary_en: B: I found no public sign of a nurse navigator for suspected lung cancer in Vantaa and Kerava or at HUS. HUS's pathway page says a doctor plans the further tests, appointments come by letter, and patients meet a nurse at the first visit for guidance. The pages do not say that a named nurse books every test, follows up on each step or prepares the multidisciplinary team meeting. A: The 2026 scoping review of 13 studies (Japan Journal of Nursing Science) says navigation was consistently linked to faster first treatment, but its abstract gives no difference against usual care. That means the assumed 15% is not confirmed.
unanswered_en: Three searches found no page from the county (vakehyva.fi) or from HUS on a named lung cancer coordinator nurse or a pilot of one, and no comparative number for the effect.
